#1 (sorry, this is my first post here, pls don't be harsh)

Everybody heard about Reynold's parametricity theorem and Wadler's theorems for free. I had spent some time trying to figure out what's the trick, and what it actually amounts to.
I believe I have an opinion on this, a rather cynical one, but maybe somebody who knows math can explain the actual meaning of it?

So far it looks to me like this: take a well-pointed category with products, exponentials (and, maybe, a classifier), map its objects to Set so that points, products, exponentials and classifier are preserved - and you get a functor. (Period.) And?
subject: Parametricity Theorem
